results.reason: Issue 3 contrasts Schedule §1.1 (ship date from Verdane's plant) with MSA §1.3 (delivery at Rochester). It explains that late-delivery measurement, risk of loss and title, and invoicing/payment all key off the ship date, so Harlow loses transit-delay remedies.
It recommends conforming Schedule §1.1 to the MSA definition (delivery at Rochester) and adding an order-of-precedence clause stating that the MSA controls over the Schedule.

Issue 2 identifies MSA §4.3's 'all housings and similar components worldwide' scope as exceeding the Term Sheet (Series 7 Housings, U.S. only). It explains that this blocks other suppliers and non-U.S. plants, and proposes narrowing language to Series 7 Housings in the U.S.

Issue 4 covers Verdane's free assignment versus Harlow's consent requirement. It notes the risk of a competitor or financially weak assignee and of access to the confidential Specifications, and recommends prior written consent, a bar on competitors, and termination on change of control.

Issue 1 explains that Amendment §2 leaves only willful misconduct outside the cap, bringing gross negligence and the IP indemnity within the 12-month fees cap. It recommends rejecting §§2.1–2.2 and keeping the original §11.2 exclusions.
The memo states that the cap is fees paid in the prior 12 months and that the original exclusions are gross negligence, willful misconduct and the §10.1 IP Indemnity.
The memo states that Term Sheet §3 limits exclusivity to Series 7 Housings in the U.S. and uses it as the baseline for comparing MSA §4.3.
The memo identifies New York law under MSA §16.1, cites no cases or statutes, and flags New York law points needing verification in its assumptions section.
The memo is addressed to the partner and ranks issues by importance. Each issue gives the location, why it matters and a recommended fix, and the memo includes an assumptions and open-facts section.
The memo explicitly says the Term Sheet is not defective and is used only as evidence of the deal. It states that the term and payment provisions match the Term Sheet and are not treated as issues.
Sections and documents are attributed consistently, with no apparent reversal of which party benefits. No legal authority is cited, and the need to verify New York law is flagged.
